title: Playing with Grover Shepard's band, his wife, and the Bucktonians
summary: Brunies and Mrs. Brunies discuss Grover Shepard's band, his saxophonist wife and where she may be found, then describe the Bucktonians, their instrumentation and bus travel to colleges.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

Oh, yeah.

And we share, we didn't have, how was it, Stump? We had drums, vocalizers. And, uh, oh, I can't think of anything. He's driving on banjo. I don't know even. And a fellow by the name of Big Boy. And a piano. Girl goes on piano. And we used to have a big bus. I used to travel from one place to the other. Especially when the colleges, the schools, you see. You get in front of a drugstore, pull out a piano, a piece and stuff, a plane, and it's all those girls coming from different places, you know. And, uh, we'd throw a sign up on the drugstore when the world was going to play out the night and they would pack them in like that.
